reason: The SQL injection is real, but the connection is read-only and the users table holds only names and e-mail addresses; the record overstates the impact.

checks.note: app/routes.py:12 reads id and app/db.py:8 formats it into the SQL text, as cited.
GET /users?id=<value> behind @login_required; any logged-in user can send it.
No binding, validation or ORM layer on the path; the only condition is a user account.
app/db.py:3 opens app.db read-only; the attacker reads names and e-mails, no secrets and no writes.
The impact is medium (other users' names and e-mails), not high.
A bound parameter enforces the invariant at the sink.

likelihood.reason: Any logged-in user can send the request.

impact.reason: The attacker reads the names and e-mail addresses of other users.
